subject: Request: bridge letter + subprocessor snapshot for DPIA walkthrough
messages:
From: Erin Cole <erin.cole@northshorebank.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: security@northshorebank.com
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPIA prep — bridge letter + subprocessor snapshot request

Hi David,

We are starting our DPIA and vendor audit prep for the new LLM integration. Security and privacy have a short list of items we need to tick off before the internal steering committee review next Thursday. Can you confirm whether you can provide the following by COB Wednesday (our time):

- A short bridge letter confirming Redwood will maintain audit access for processors listed in the DPA during the onboarding period (we'll need a DocuSign-ready draft).
- A current subprocessor snapshot (names, roles, region, contractual status) and an explicit callout of any subprocessors located outside the EU/UK.
- An extract of Art. 30 records for processing activities relevant to Northshore (sample CSV is fine).
- A sample KMS access log (redacted) showing key usage for a recent 7-day window.

We may request a short walkthrough (30–45m) of the evidence after we receive the docs. Please cc your privacy contact and legal.

Thanks,
Erin Cole
Head of Vendor Risk
Northshore Bank

[Attachment: NSB_DPIA_Checklist.pdf]

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Erin Cole <erin.cole@northshorebank.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPIA prep — bridge letter + subprocessor snapshot request

Erin — thanks for the clear list. We can get a majority of this to you by EOD Wednesday (your time); a couple of clarifications below to make sure we scope the artifacts correctly: 

1) Bridge letter: we have a standard draft that confirms audit access and lines up with our DPA. I'll attach the draft (DocuSign-ready) and can revise the language if you need explicit references to Art. 28/30.

2) Subprocessor snapshot: we'll provide a CSV export with current subprocessors, their role (hosting, logging, monitoring), country, and whether they process cardholder or account identifiers. If a party is outside the EU/UK we'll call that out with the transfer mechanism.

3) Art. 30 extract: we'll deliver a scoped extract covering the Northshore-related processing activities and retention terms.

4) KMS sample: we will provide a redacted sample of key-usage logs (timestamps, operation type, region) — note that full plaintext access logs are restricted; we will provide a secure-read sample.

Attachments I'll include in the next email: subprocessor snapshot export and bridge letter draft. Can you confirm the audience for the walkthrough (legal, infosec, privacy) and any IP restrictions on screenshots? We will provision a read-only evidence view in our secure portal.

Best,
David Kim
Security & Privacy Lead
Redwood Inference

[Attachment stubs referenced: subprocessor_snapshot_20270316.csv, redwood_bridge_letter_draft.pdf]

From: Erin Cole <erin.cole@northshorebank.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: security@northshorebank.com
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPIA prep — bridge letter + subprocessor snapshot request

Thanks David — that sounds good. A few follow-ups so we can triage internally: 

- Please explicitly mark any subprocessors that perform ‘inference-time storage’ vs 'model hosting' — the reviewers treat those differently.
- If you have any subprocessors that are US-based with data transfer reliance on SCCs or other safeguards, call those out.
- For the Art. 30 extract, include the legal basis you list for each activity where possible and the retention period.
- On KMS logs: we only need a redacted sample; please remove any principal identifiers.

Audience for walkthrough: privacy, vendor risk, and one member of our cloud security team (total 4). Screenshots are fine in the secure session; we just prefer no screenshots included in the PDF artifacts themselves.

If you can send the artifacts by Wednesday morning CET, we will review and propose a slot for the walkthrough on Thursday afternoon CET.

Regards,
Erin

[On Tue, Mar 16, 2027 at 10:05 AM David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> Erin — thanks for the clear list...]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Erin Cole <erin.cole@northshorebank.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 09:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPIA prep — bridge letter + subprocessor snapshot request

Hi Erin — copying in a few clarifications from legal/privacy to help the review: 

- Subprocessor roles: our CSV will include a role column with values such as Hosting, Logging/Observability, KMS, Monitoring, and Model Fine-tuning. We will add a separate flag "inference-time storage" for any processors that temporarily persist inference outputs.
- Transfers: any transfer outside the UK/EU will be annotated with the transfer mechanism (SCCs, adequacy, or derogation). We currently have two subprocessors in the US that operate logging pipelines (SCCs active); none of the core model weights are hosted outside EU for the Northshore deployment.
- Art. 30: our extract will include the activity description, categories of data subject/data, retention, legal basis, and subprocessors involved.
- KMS logs: we will provide a 7-day redacted TSV sample; access to the full logs needs a read-only session request to preserve operational controls.

We will also include a short, one-page cover note describing scope and limitations of the artifacts (useful for your steering committee).

I'll attach the Art. 30 extract and the KMS sample in the secure portal; David will upload the CSV snapshot and the bridge-letter draft to DocuSign.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference

[Attachment stubs: art30-extract-20270316.csv, kms_access_log_sample.tsv]
